target_customer: Hardware companies building electronic products, including aerospace and defense teams needing compliant supply chains
problem: Hardware teams manage bills of materials and component purchasing with spreadsheets and shelves, causing delays in sourcing and production.
business_model: B2B software plus procurement execution and ITAR-registered warehousing and kitting services

founders.name: Matthew Haber
previous_startups: BeSide (R&D and product design company, acquired by a private equity backed buyer, per YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page describes engineering, technology leadership and design background.

founders.name: Phillip Gulley
education: MFA, Brooklyn College (Performance and Interactive Media Arts)
previous_startups: Co-founded an R&D, product design and experiential company that was acquired (per YC page)

competitors.name: Octopart
competitors.what: Electronic component search engine and BOM tool

technical_complexity.rationale: Aggregating component and supplier data, procurement execution and compliant warehousing combine software with physical logistics operations.

defensibility.rationale: ITAR registered warehousing, supplier relationships and integration into customers' BOM workflow are harder to copy than software alone.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge in the sources found; Cofactr itself acquired Factor.io in February 2025.

market_need_then: Hardware teams relied on spreadsheets for BOMs and the 2021 to 2022 component shortage made sourcing painful (inferred from the company's positioning; no dated source quantifying demand was read).

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and playful: From BOM to Build, Get to the Good Parts

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: Get to the Good Parts
branding.community_and_virality: Company runs a podcast and newsletter per its site; no third party brand coverage found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear taglines and owned content channels, a registered trademark in 2025, but confusable with Cofactor Genomics in search results.

outcome_analysis: Cofactr raised a seed led by Bain Capital Ventures after YC Winter 2022 and a 17.2M USD Series A led by Bain Capital in December 2024, bringing total funding to about 28.8M USD per press. It bought Factor.io in February 2025 and added ITAR warehousing, which fits demand from aerospace and defense customers like Stoke Space. It remains independent and active.
notes: Seed: YC page cites a TechCrunch article dated 2022-11-28 on the seed; the 6M USD amount, SAFE with 25M cap and investor list come from a search snippet of that article, with a Clay aggregator saying about 6.15M in April 2022; the link above is the TechCrunch post id seen in results and was not opened. Total funding 28.8M minus 17.2M leaves about 11.6M not explained by the 6M seed, so earlier rounds may be missing (partial). Seedtable names Squadra Ventures as Series A lead, conflicting with Bain Capital in press releases; press favoured. Businesswire fetch returned 403; Series A confirmed through the company press page and multiple outlets in search. Octopart date is its 2015 acquisition, not a source from the batch. Haber education not found.
